finalText:
In the current revision (Rev. 4), SP 800-63B sets requirements for all ten topics. I read them on the official NIST page, https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html. The relevant text is in §3.1.1.1 (Password Authenticators) and §3.1.1.2 (Password Verifiers). I did not open Rev. 3, so I haven't compared it with the earlier text.

- **Minimum length:** Passwords used as the only factor SHALL be at least 15 characters. Passwords used only as part of multi-factor authentication MAY be shorter, but SHALL be at least 8 characters.
- **Maximum length:** Verifiers SHOULD permit at least 64 characters. This is a SHOULD, not a SHALL.
- **Composition rules, periodic change, hints and security questions:** All four are SHALL NOT. The one exception is that a verifier SHALL force a change if the authenticator may be compromised.
- **Blocklist:** Verifiers SHALL compare a new password against a blocklist of commonly used, expected or compromised passwords.
- **Password managers:** Verifiers SHALL allow password managers and autofill.
- **Salt:** The salt SHALL be at least 32 bits.
- **Hashing scheme:** This is only a SHOULD. The page says an approved scheme from the latest revision of SP 800-132 "SHOULD be used". Separately, passwords SHALL be salted and hashed with a suitable password hashing scheme.
